what_to_detect: A triggered ability that went on the stack leaves it by resolving, after players could respond to it; the cost half's outcome is resolved and the acting line is a trigger line.
near_miss: A triggered ability on the stack is countered by a response (outcome countered) and does not resolve.
record_fields: ability provenance key trait_kind (trigger vs spell/activated)

what_to_detect: A zone-change trigger's resolution finds its triggering object in the zone the trigger names as its destination and acts on it: the effect half holds a zone_change of that object whose from_zone is the trigger's Destination$.
near_miss: A zone-change trigger's resolution whose object left the zone it moved to finds nothing, and its effect half holds no event for that object.
record_fields: acting line root Mode$ and Destination$ via the sidecar

what_to_detect: An Aura's trigger on its enchanted permanent leaving the battlefield resolves and acts on the Aura's new object in its owner's graveyard: the effect half holds a zone_change from Graveyard whose subject is the trigger's own source card.
near_miss: The same kind of Aura trigger whose Aura is no longer in the graveyard when it resolves, so its effect half holds no move of the Aura.
record_fields: acting line root Mode$ and ValidCard$ via the sidecar

what_to_detect: A delayed triggered ability created by a resolving spell or ability is evaluated when its trigger event later occurs and fires once (trigger record fired=true whose trait was spawned by a DelayedTrigger segment or an AtEOT$ parameter of the acting line). A delayed trigger is engine-built and keys to the line of the ability that spawned it, whose root segment is that spell or ability (no Mode$), so trigger_mode's mode parameter, which reads the root Mode$, cannot select it.
near_miss: The same delayed trigger evaluated at a later occurrence of its event after it has already triggered once does not fire.
record_fields: acting line script_text segments (DelayedTrigger, AtEOT$) via the sidecar

what_to_detect: A delayed triggered ability is evaluated only for trigger events occurring after it was created, and fires on the first such event (trigger record fired=true for a trait spawned by a DelayedTrigger segment or AtEOT$ parameter). A delayed trigger is engine-built and keys to the line of the ability that spawned it, whose root segment is that spell or ability (no Mode$), so trigger_mode's mode parameter, which reads the root Mode$, cannot select it.
near_miss: A delayed trigger created after its trigger event (such as the beginning of a step) already happened is not evaluated for that event; its first evaluation is at the next occurrence.
record_fields: turn and step of the spawning resolution against the trigger record
acting line script_text segments via the sidecar

what_to_detect: A delayed triggered ability that refers to a particular object resolves and acts on it while it is still in the zone it is expected to be in: the effect half of the delayed trigger's resolution holds an event for that object.
near_miss: The same kind of delayed trigger resolves after its object left the expected zone (and possibly returned as a new object); its effect half holds no event for the object.
record_fields: acting line script_text segments (DelayedTrigger, AtEOT$) via the sidecar

what_to_detect: A reflexive 'when you do' triggered ability created during a resolution triggers because the stated action happened during that resolution (trigger record fired=true for a trait spawned by an ImmediateTrigger segment). A reflexive trigger is engine-built by an ImmediateTrigger segment and keys to the line holding that segment, whose root Mode$ is the parent ability's (ChangesZone, Attacks ...), so trigger_mode's mode parameter cannot select Immediate.
near_miss: The resolution's instructed action does not happen, so the reflexive trigger does not trigger; Forge then builds no reflexive trigger, so the near miss shows only as the parent resolution with no such trigger record after it.
record_fields: acting line script_text segments (ImmediateTrigger) via the sidecar
the parent resolution record (game_id, timestamp order)

what_to_detect: A reflexive triggered ability whose trigger is paying a cost that may be paid several times triggers once however many times the cost was paid (one trigger record fired=true for a trait spawned by an ImmediateTrigger segment per parent resolution). A reflexive trigger is engine-built by an ImmediateTrigger segment and keys to the line holding that segment, whose root Mode$ is the parent ability's (ChangesZone, Attacks ...), so trigger_mode's mode parameter cannot select Immediate.
near_miss: The cost is paid zero times, so the reflexive trigger does not trigger and no trigger record follows the parent resolution.
record_fields: acting line script_text segments (ImmediateTrigger) via the sidecar
count of such trigger records per parent resolution (game_id, timestamp)
